dedupe_keys.name: who unicef jmp global database on drinking water sanitation and hygiene

description: The JMP global database holds the official estimates of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene for every country, compiled by the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme, the custodian of Sustainable Development Goal 6 targets on water, sanitation and hygiene. It draws on nearly 9,000 national datasets such as household surveys and censuses to produce estimates for 237 countries, areas and territories. The household database covers progress since 2000, a schools database started in 2018 and a health care facility database in 2019, with service ladders from safely managed to no service, urban and rural splits and, where data permit, subnational and wealth inequalities. Estimates are annual at national level with regional and global aggregates, updated every two years. Data can be explored online as charts, tables and maps, or downloaded free as Excel files per country, region or the world. No licence is displayed next to the files, while JMP reports use Creative Commons IGO licences, so reuse terms should be checked. Caveats: values are modelled from surveys of varying age and quality, and they describe service access, not network assets. Simulation uses: setting baseline service levels and vulnerable populations for water and sanitation resilience, emergency response and investment scenarios, and checking whether health care facilities have water and sanitation. Related records: national performance data such as Brazil's SNIS (data-brazil-snis-sanitation-information-system) and Australia's National Performance Report (data-bom-national-performance-report-urban-water) give utility-level detail.
